Our platform seamlessly connects your people, machinery and actions with data, leading to more efficient operations. Clients tell us that implementing our software feels like their data-congested brain finally gets the much-needed neurological wiring that prompts action. Finally, you understand what is happening. Finally, you know what to do next. Finally, you can act confidently.

name: Luo Automation
description: To guarantee patient safety, every single injectable medicine must be visually inspected. Therefore, hospital pharmacies and pharmaceutical companies check every vial, syringe or ampoule to make sure it’s free of defects. Defects can be contaminations such as glass or steel particles, but can also be a broken cap, a big crack or a small dent. In general, this visual inspection is done by hand. Every container must be evaluated for 10 seconds by a trained operator. For companies that produce big batches and lots of similar products (more than 5 million containers per year) it’s feasible to automate this process. To do so, expensive machinery (>2M euro) is bought, an extensive training process is started and after the installation and validation process, one or two products can be visually inspected. However, lots of companies do not produce enough containers per year to account a 2M euro investment or have a very diverse product portfolio, which makes current machinery not suitable. As a result, in Europe more than 1.2 billion containers are checked by hand. Every year. Luo tries to bridge the gap between huge, conservative and expensive machinery and the manual operation. Besides developing the hardware (machine) that is needed to gather the necessary data of every container, Luo uses different AI and Machine Learning models to analyze this data and define if the container is good or needs to be rejected. One of the key challenges in this field, is that defect data of syringes, ampoules and vials is barely available. Even if a decent defect set is available for one specific medicine in one specific container with one specific filling volume, this is not applicable on other medicines or other containers. Luo is using innovative training methods to make sure we are able to find defects the algorithm has never seen before. For the visual inspection of one container, about 8 (!) different anomaly detection models are used. These models are trained with normal data, to make sure the models are not dependent on defect data. By using these innovative models, we are able quickly adapt to new medicine or new containers. As a result, it’s feasible to automate the obligatory visual inspection for small batches or a diverse product portfolio as well. Besides saving a lot of valuable time of healthcare professionals, this increase the consistency and quality of the product and provides insights in production quality over time.
